'Incredible achievement for the family' as Bellingham brothers called up
item.description: Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since the Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago [Getty Images] It may be a surprise to some but Jobe Bellingham's call up to the England senior side has been a long time coming. Just like his older brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players - Jobe's career path has been very similar. He too was a star of the Birmingham City academy before making a big-money move to the German Bundesliga and getting an England call-up. Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days. He was 69 days older than when Jude made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side. The centre midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to £31m. Jude also moved to the German Club, when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid. Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling. But the former Sunderland midfielder is his own player and wears 'Jobe' on the back of his shirt instead of his family name and said that it was suggested to him by a former coach because "it shows that I'm going my own way". Jobe is a different type of player to Jude, sitting deeper in the midfield but is as physically imposing while still being good on the ball. He is the current captain of the England U21 side and England manager Thomas Tuchel said the Young Lions head coach Lee Carsley had been pushing for some time for the younger Bellingham to get senior recognition. "He's the standout player. He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time," said Tuchel. "That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential." England host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before travelling to Madrid to take on Spain on 15 November in this next international break. With Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, and Bournemouth's Alex Scott out injured after shining on his debut in last month's 7-0 win over Croatia, Tuchel said that a natural "opportunity" for Jobe had opened up. "He deserves to make an impression for us," said the German in his news conference after naming the squad. "It's an incredible achievement for the family and for the brothers. I saw his excitement straight away and his smile. "He has an open and calm personality. He's one of five players for the central midfield. "He's a more defensive player than Jude. item.title: Northamptonshire all-rounder Kimber extends deal
item.description: Louis Kimber was part of the Northamptonshire Steelbacks side that won the 2026 T20 Blast [Getty Images] Northamptonshire all-rounder Louis Kimber has signed a one-year contract extension that will keep him with the county until the end of the 2028 season. The 29-year-old joined the club from Leicestershire last year and played 17 matches across the County Championship and T20 Blast, which Northamptonshire won in July. Kimber hit a best of 66 in Northants' win at Gloucestershire in May and has scored a total of 1,685 first-class runs. "Winning the Blast was an incredible achievement, and one that has made us even hungrier for success," Kimber told the club's website. "I can't wait to get back to work, continue improving my game and contribute even more success for the club." Kimber took just one wicket and hit 175 runs in his first season with Northants but head coach Darren Lehmann believes more is to come. "Louis maybe didn't have the season he'd have liked this year, but I believe he is a player that can make a big contribution to the side," Lehmann said. "I'm really looking forward to seeing Louis showcase what he can do next year."

Minnesota suffered their first loss of the season in Week 8 and now faces another elite team in Buffalo. To make matters worse, the Vikings will be forced to start Carson Wentz against the Bills on Sunday. Wentz explained his perspective on one key problem surrounding the offense during a recent interview. He has a plan for getting Justin Jefferson more involved in the passing game. “I mean, just get him the rock. He’s as good as I’ve been around. So, you know, for him the last couple of weeks not getting it as much as he would maybe want, I get it. I’d be frustrated if I were him,” Wentz told reporters on Thursday, per Ari Meirov. “I mean, he’s as good as it gets at his position and I look forward to just, I want to get him the rock as much as anybody. I look forward to trying to do that without forcing it. We’ve got a bunch of talent on the offensive side of the ball, so my job is just to distribute it and I’m confident he’ll get his this week.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kyler Murray is dealing with a sore hamstring, which is why Wentz will get the start. Jefferson and Murray have not created a very strong chemistry between the two. The superstar receiver only has 28 receptions for 335 yards and four touchdowns in six games this season. He has yet to go over 100 yards in a game and has only received 40 targets thus far. It is great to hear that Wentz will prioritize getting Jefferson involved. Jefferson stiffed the media last week and seemed frustrated with Murray’s performance in their loss to Detroit. Fly-half Smith fit to steer England against Wallabies
item.description: Smith overtook George Ford in the fly-half pecking order during this year's Six Nations [Getty Images] Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury to start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday. Smith has started England's past five matches at 10, but was a doubt to face the Wallabies in the Nations Championship encounter after coming off late on in club side Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October. The 24-year-old is joined in the starting line-up by flanker Ben Curry, who makes his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months. Curry, whose twin brother Tom suffered an injury set-back in training earlier this week that took him out of contention, is seen as key to combatting Australia's breakdown specialists Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano and ensuring a supply of quick ball to Smith and his backline. Smith will have Saints team-mate Tommy Freeman as an attacking outlet and a target for crossfield kicks on the wing, while full-back George Furbank, who can step in at first receiver, played alongside both before his summer move to Harlequins. Alex Coles, another Northampton player, wins a starting second row spot ahead of George Martin, while Henry Slade is chosen at outside centre, with no space for either Joe Marchant or Will Joseph in the matchday 23. Fin Baxter, who only made two appearances since a comeback from a 10-month foot-injury lay-off, is the starting loose-head prop, with Ellis Genge poised on the bench alongside Will Stuart, another welcome front-row returnee. Exeter back row Greg Fisilau is poised to win his first cap after being named on the bench. item.description: ORCHARD PARK - At least this time the Buffalo Bills had ample time to adjust their defensive game plan in the wake of a seismic shift in their opponent’s quarterback situation. Thursday, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell announced that Kyler Murray would not play in Monday night’s showdown against the Bills in a battle of two 6-1, division-leading teams. The mobile Murray has a hamstring injury, so immobile backup Carson Wentz takes over. But given how the Bills responded last Sunday when they spent nearly two weeks preparing to face Baltimore’s dynamic Lamar Jackson, only to see him leave after the very first play , head coach Joe Brady believes his defense will adapt without a problem. “Defensively, I think they had to have the mindset of getting ready for both of them as well,” Brady said, indicating the Bills were well aware even early in the practice week that Murray might not play. “Carson Wentz has played games this year, he's played really good football in the league for a long time, but obviously there's always going to be a little bit of adjustment with different types of skill sets. We found out last week, you're having to make adjustments in game on the second play, right, so nothing that Jim (Leonhard) and his staff is not used to.” What’s interesting is that while the Ravens were a shell of themselves without Jackson, the Vikings may be better off with Wentz because Murray has not been effective in his first season with Minnesota. Wentz replaced an injured Murray early in the season opener and helped lead a comeback win against the Packers, then started in a Week 2 victory over the Bears before Murray returned to action in Week 3. To be fair, Wentz wasn’t all that much better than Murray and regardless of who has been the QB, the Vikings’ offense has been pretty putrid as it ranks 27th in scoring (20.0 points per game), 29th in total yards (279.4) and 31st in passing yards (165.6). Not even a game against the Lions ’ awful defense could help the Vikings last week in their 19-15 loss, but now they’ll get a crack at another of the NFL’s weakest defenses, this time at home, and perhaps Wentz’s steadier hand will make a difference. “He is the perfect guy in a moment where you can't have Kyler out there at full strength to go in there," O'Connell said. "And we feel very strongly about when Carson's in there, we're going to get really effective quarterback play." item.title: The breakdown battle that could decide England vs Australia
item.description: It is about eight months since England’s men last trod the Twickenham turf, a long gap between hit-outs on home soil. That performance against Ireland will carry few happy memories for Steve Borthwick ’s squad – not that there is any conscious effort to right the wrongs. “If we’re going to sit and stew over a game eight months ago, we’re in f***** trouble,” a surprisingly spiky Richard Wigglesworth, the senior assistant coach, remarked this week. Still, England would be wise to reflect on their failings in that game. While there was plenty to learn from a lean Six Nations, it was that showing in the 42-21 defeat that most disappointed Borthwick and his selection, falling so far short of where they needed to be . It was at the breakdown where Ireland beasted them particularly, and in the two red zones especially: Andy Farrell’s side won 14 turnovers and limited England to just 1.3 points per 22 entry. England were heavily beaten by Ireland in the Six Nations (PA Wire) England’s difficulty at the breakdown was striking given their selection. That game remains Henry Pollock ’s only start at Test level; a back row of he, Tom Curry and Ben Earl should have provided plenty of ruck menace. But, perhaps, Borthwick was guilty of a redundancy of skillset. While Pollock and Earl are enterprising and prolific carriers, neither is a consistent resourcer of rucks; Curry, too, per Opta hit just 11.7 rucks per 80 minutes for Sale across the last Prem campaign, less than half that of Guy Pepper, a significant absentee for this campaign. That may be partly to do with Bath’s multi-phase preference, and also Curry’s usage as an edge forward in attack. Guy Pepper is a significant absentee (PA Wire) But against Ireland, England lacked big bodies in the tight exchanges, and found themselves bedevilled by Tadhg Beirne, Caelan Doris, Dan Sheehan and Josh van der Flier. It is notable that Borthwick, even with Pepper and Tom Curry injured, has not elected to pair Earl and Pollock again – the pair perhaps better dovetail in the second half, when the game loses some structure and each can use their athleticism to collect a volume of carries. Since his installation on the blindside for the France game in March, Ollie Chessum has provided better balance around the park and more variety at the lineout from which to launch. The inclusion of Ben Curry, who returns for a first England appearance since July 2025, provides the side with perhaps their best pure jackaller – even if his twin brother’s ability to steal time and bodies with ruck hustle will be missed. item.title: Trainer trifecta on tap with British Isles-bred horses in Melbourne Cup
item.description: Lambeth, shown winning the October 9 Sycamore Stakes at Keeneland, is the early favorite for Saturday's Grade III River City at Churchill Downs. Photo courtesy of Keeneland Oct. 6 (UPI) -- Tuesday's Melbourne Cup, inconveniently scheduled just three days after the Breeders' Cup, produced a trifecta win for trainer Ciaron Maher and for horses bred in the British Isles. Next up are the Japan Cup, with the Aga Khan's Studs' Calandagan hoping to double up on his historic victory a year ago, and then Hong Kong's iconic year-end international races with big names from around the world in the early-entry box. Back in North America, horse racing catches its breath after another successful return of the Breeders Cup to Keeneland. Around the world, around the clock Australia It's unusual to see a trainer saddle the first three finishers in any race, much less a top-level race (think Aidan O'Brien and Chad Brown). But how about "the race that stops the nation" -- the Melbourne Cup? That's the hat trick that Ciaron Maher pulled off Tuesday at Flemington. Point of Law went off favorite at 6-1 and showed that was value, winning by 3 3/4 lengths from 25-1 stablemate Zahrann. Juja Kibo completed the hat trick, just a nose farther behind. The closest rival was the Joseph O'Brien shipper Sons and Lovers, another 1 1/4 lengths in arrears. Maher had a strong hand with seven horses in the field of 23, also including Royal Supremacy, who shot away to a gigantic lead before handing over to his stablemate. The trainer became the first to score the Melbourne Cup trifecta. "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute," Maher said in post-race interview. "I certainly didn't know that Royal Supremacy would lead by that far, but it is a true test of staying and, Point of Law, he's just thrived. "It has been a whirlwind, but I'm very proud of all the team to get three horses in the first three spots." While the results were a sweep for the home team, it's worth noting that all three top finishers were sired by European-raced stallions -- Frankel, Night of Thunder and Belardo -- and bred in the British Isles. Point of Law was bred in England by King Charles III and raced there in the royal colors through the summer under the care of John and Thady Gosden before changing hands to an Aussie syndicate. Zahrann and Juba Kibo were bred in Ireland. Zahrann raced in Ireland through 2025, and Juba Kibo is the only horse of the first three whose career has been run solely down under. Trainer trifectas in big races? Aidan O'Brien was 1-2-3 in the 2016 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with Found, Highland Reel and Order of St George and 1-2-3 in the 2020 Breeders' Cup Mile with Order of Australia, Circus Maximus and Lope y Fernandez -- a trifecta that returned $4,393 for a 50-cent investment. item.title: Fin Smith wins fitness race as England hand out debut in Australia clash
item.description: Fin Smith has won his fitness race to start at fly half for England against Australia, with Greg Fisilau primed for a debut from the bench. Smith had been a doubt with a calf injury but has been named at No 10 against the Wallabies having come through training this week. Full-back George Furbank returns to the side for the first time since November 2024 , while Ben Curry starts on the openside with twin brother Tom ruled out. Fisilau and Henry Pollock provide back row cover from the bench with Ollie Chessum continuing in his blindside flanker role. Loosehead prop Fin Baxter starts on his Test return from a long-term lay-off with a complex foot injury, while Maro Itoje captains the side having been rested during the first phase of the Nations Championship. “Australia are a talented side who have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months,” said head coach Steve Borthwick. “We know the challenge that awaits us and we’re looking forward to it. “We’re excited to be playing in front of our home supporters and to start an important block of games. This will also be our last opportunity to face southern hemisphere opposition at home before the World Cup next year.” Furbank’s return comes after a horror run of injuries that has included a broken arm, concussion and a calf issue. The 30-year-old was due to feature against South Africa in July before requiring emergency appendix surgery in Johannesburg. England also face Japan and New Zealand this November , as well as an unconfirmed opposition on the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium. Australia spring a selection surprise with lock Jeremy Williams shifted to the blindside flank, while Declan Meredith is preferred to Ben Donaldson at fly half. item.title: What happened to Jack Grealish? From Man City's £100m treble hero to Everton outcast
item.description: What happened to Jack Grealish? From Man City's £100m treble hero to Everton outcast originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As England retreated further and further into their defensive shell, virtually demanding that Argentina put them out of their World Cup semifinal misery, everyone had an opinion on what the problem was and what Thomas Tuchel should do. The Three Lions boss' decision to leave several high-quality players at home felt like it came home to roost as his team fell under Lionel Messi's spell and lost 2-1 from 1-0 up in Atlanta . For those who spent plenty of time watching Pep Guardiola's treble-winning Manchester City side come together and hit top gear in 2022-23, one name that had fallen some way off the radar came to mind. England could really have done with a fit and focused Jack Grealish. From being a cult hero at boyhood club Aston Villa , Grealish joined City for a British-record £100 million in summer 2021. After a first season of acclimatization, he became integral to Guardiola's winning machine. Few players anywhere had his capacity to take possession, hold it and cherish it; get the team up the pitch and make the right decision to either relieve pressure or keep attacks rumbling. England still don't have one of those players, as evidenced by the squad Tuchel announced on Friday for the November internationals. Manchester City don't, particularly, nowadays. Everton do, on loan from City, but have won their past two games with him banished from the squad. MORE: Jack Grealish and Man City: What went wrong for £100m star? Why is Jack Grealish not playing for Everton? Grealish did not feature in Everton's 2-0 defeat away to Premier League champions Arsenal on October 24 due to illness. Five days later, he was unavailable for the 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United "due to a breach of club discipline." The 31-year-old remained sidelined for Monday's 1-0 league win at Newcastle and will not be involved when David Moyes' side welcome Coventry City to the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. “Jack’s not available,” Moyes said at his pre-match news conference. "I wouldn’t give you the plan, but we will be working with Jack again soon.” Asked whether Grealish was presently at the club, Moyes added: “I would rather not answer your question. Right from the start, hopefully you picked up on my words. I said it was a club issue and it continues to be that.” What's gone wrong for Jack Grealish? Everton have kept communications tight publicly around the Grealish issue, while acknowledging that this is not simply a call from Moyes and that the Merseyside club's hierarchy are very much involved. item.title: Mikel Arteta offers Ezri Konsa update after Arsenal injury scare
item.description: Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Ezri Konsa was withdrawn against Slavia Prague on Wednesday as a “precaution” but is confident the Arsenal centre-back will be available to face Hull on Saturday. Konsa has been a standout in the Arsenal defence since his arrival from Aston Villa in the summer, stepping up in the absence of William Saliba and keeping four Premier League sheets in a row. The England international was replaced by Cristhian Mosquera in the 61st minute in the Champions League in Czechia but Arteta said it was only due to managing his workload before the international break. “He's fine,” Arteta confirmed at a press conference on Friday. “He was feeling much better today. We took him out for a precaution and for the amount of minutes that he is playing, but yesterday and today, he's feeling good." Centre-back Saliba has not featured yet this season but nearing a return for Arsenal and was part of their squad in the Champions League in midweek. Arteta confirmed that Arsenal are in contact with France and their new manager Zinedine Zidane , and are hopeful the Premier League winning defender will not be called up by Les Bleues this month. item.title: Women's rights matter more than any league, say Afghan cricketers
item.description: Firooza Amiri and Nahida Sapan were among the Afghan women's players to flee to Australia [Getty Images] Afghan women's cricketers have accused overseas players signing up for the inaugural Afghanistan Premier League of sending a message to the world that women suffering in the country "can simply be ignored". Women's participation in sport has been effectively outlawed since the Taliban's return to power in 2021, and many of Afghanistan's female cricketers left the country for their own safety. The men's franchise league is expected to start in December in the UAE, though it is yet to be sanctioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC). In September, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) urged players to reconsider their involvement and batter Ollie Pope withdrew. "For five years, girls in Afghanistan have been denied the right to play cricket and many other basic rights," Nahida Sapan, who captained the Afghanistan Refugee Women's XI on this summer's tour of England, told the BBC Stumped podcast . "Foreign players had a real opportunity to stand with millions of Afghan women and girls by choosing not to participate. "It may have seemed like a small action, but it could have sent a powerful message and put pressure on those responsible. "This is not about being against cricket or Afghan men's cricket. It is about standing up for basic human rights." Eight English players were signed in the draft on Tuesday, alongside players from Scotland, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand. England's Alex Hales, Tymal Mills, Joe Clarke, Olly Stone, Moeen Ali, Luke Wood, Tom Moores and Chris Wood were all signed. Scotland's George Munsey also secured a deal, as did Ireland all-rounder Curtis Campher. Other England players including Dawid Malan and James Vince also put their names into the draft. England will have more overseas representation than any other country in the Afghan league. The major names signed from other nations include Sri Lanka internationals Kusal Perera, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera and Kamindu Mendis, Australian batter D'Arcy Short, South Africa spinner Imran Tahir and Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan. The ECB has refused to schedule bilateral cricket with Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power - a stance Australia also adopts. England have, however, continued to play against Afghanistan at global events, including World Cups in both limited-overs formats and the Champions Trophy, which resulted in calls from MPs for their game in 2025 to be boycotted. "For me, the women and girls of Afghanistan come first," said Sapan. "Their rights, dignity and freedom matter more than any league or sporting opportunity. "Taking part in this league without acknowledging what is happening to Afghan women risks sending the message to the world that their suffering can simply be ignored." item.title: Oxford City can shock Leicester - Foxes fan Pollock
item.description: Scott Pollock previously played for Brackley Town, where he made 70 appearances [Getty Images] Oxford City midfielder Scott Pollock believes there is "no reason" his side cannot pile more pressure on his beloved Leicester City by pulling off an FA Cup upset when they host the Foxes on Friday night. The National League North side welcome the former Premier League and FA Cup winners to The MGroup Stadium in the first round of this season's competition, under the lights on their artificial pitch. Pollock, who joined the non-leaguers in July, is relishing coming up against his boyhood club, who he supports and tried out for as a youngster. "It just felt like it was meant to be as a Leicester fan myself," he told BBC Radio Oxford. "Away (from home) would have been nice but I feel that at home we have a good chance of going through. "I had trials with Leicester as a goalkeeper when I was younger and they turned me down, it was then after that I decided to be an outfield player." From playing against Messi and Ronaldo to non-league Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City Oxford City have made it to the first round proper for the first time in four years, having narrowly beaten Torquay United in the final qualifying round. Pollock, 25, has personal experience of an Oxford City shock. He was a Northampton Town player in 2020 when the part-time Hoops beat their League One opponents 2-1 in an FA Cup giant-killing. And he believes the pressure is all on the third-tier Foxes, who have struggled in their start to the League One campaign following back-to-back relegations from the Premier League and the Championship. "There's just a feeling of excitement among us really," Pollock added. "The pressure's on them to do well in the league and in the cup - we're at home and we know the pitch so it favours us in that aspect. "That being said, we know they're a good team so we have to be up for it. Oxford City have done cup upsets before and there is no reason why we can't do it again." From Youtube to playing on TV in the FA Cup Pollock has had a somewhat unique footballing journey, first making a name for himself on YouTube with Hashtag United. Spencer Owen co-founded Hashtag with his brother Seb Carmichael-Brown in 2016 and ran an academy series on their channel in 2017. Pollock ended up winning the series and then played for their first team, starring in a charity game called the Wembley Cup where he won man of the match and was rewarded with a trial at Premier League side Crystal Palace. A year later he moved to Northampton, where he made 29 senior appearances, scoring two goals. "They were trying to find the next star," he recalled of the Hashtag series, having applied for it when he was just 16. "I didn't think anything of it when I applied for it and I ended up winning it out of 20,000 people. "It was a good experience when I was younger and I got to play men's football from a young age so it's helped a lot in my career."

item.title: Iraola calls for a Liverpool reaction as defensive set-piece woes raise fresh concerns
item.description: Iraola calls for a Liverpool reaction as defensive set-piece woes raise fresh concerns Andoni Iraola has demanded that Liverpool react to recent setbacks against Arsenal and Fenerbahce. Liverpool travel to Crystal Palace in the Premier League this weekend after successive defeats. Last season, Liverpool led the Premier League for set-piece goals conceded (20), while Iraola's Bournemouth side ranked second (18). The Spaniard said his team must show a reaction as the Reds look to remain within reach of the teams at the top. "I think that is the challenge, especially in a club like Liverpool. item.description: Manchester United will be without Carlos Baleba for several weeks due to the hamstring injury he suffered against Roma. item.title: Pirates Free Agent Needs: Could Bucs Add Another Leverage Reliever?
item.description: The Pirates appear to have one of the more formidable setup man/closer duos for 2027 in Mason Montgomery and Luke Weaver. Montgomery cemented himself as the team’s closer after dominating down the stretch. Weaver was acquired by the Mets at the deadline and is under contractual control for next season. The back of the bullpen is strong. But could the Pirates add another leverage or late-inning reliever to the mix? It might not be the most pressing need, but Ben Cherington certainly learned his lesson about the importance of a strong and deep bullpen after last year’s showing. If the Pirates opt to pursue adding a leverage reliever, it would likely be someone who wouldn’t break the bank. Guys like Adrián Morejón and David Bednar are good fits on paper but will be too expensive for Pittsburgh. Here are some more affordable alternatives who could make sense. RHP Evan Phillips 2026 stats: 3-2, 3.46 ERA, 26 innings, 22 hits, six walks, 33 strikeouts, one save, 31 appearaces Phillips might end up getting a contract too rich for the Pirates. But the 32-year-old has been extremely effective for the Dodgers when healthy. From 2023-24, Phillips recorded 42 saves. RHP Bryan Abreu 2026 stats: 6-4, 3.73 ERA, 62.2 innings, 44 hits, 41 walks, 80 strikeouts, nine saves, 66 appearances Abreu had been one of the more effective and durable relievers in the league entering the season. From 2022-25, he made 275 appearances and had a 2.30 ERA. But the 29-year-old took a step back this year, largely due to high walk totals. Abreu was still effective, though. RHP Emilio Pagán 2026 stats: 5-1, 3.38 ERA, 42.2 innings, 33 hits, 11 walks, 45 strikeouts, 25 saves, 45 appearances Pagán has been with the Reds the last three years and has served as closer for the last two, so the Pirates have seen a lot of him. The 35-year-old has combined for 57 saves since the start of the 2025 season. RHP Jonathan Loáisiga 2026 stats: 7-3, 2.42 ERA, 67 innings, 56 hits, 13 walks, 48 strikeouts, two saves, 67 appearances A career Yankee up until this season, Loáisiga thrived in his first year with the Diamondbacks. The just-turned 32-year-old spent most of his time pitching in the seventh, eighth and ninth innings and largely handled big spots in the game. RHP Kevin Ginkel 2026 stats: 6-4, 4.12 ERA, 67.2 innings, 59 hits, 17 walks, 72 strikeouts, three saves, 74 appearances Another Diamondback, only three relievers in the National League made more appearances than Ginkel. While the 32-year-old’s ERA is a bit high, he pairs it with a more reasonable 3.50 FIP. Of anyone on this list, he will probably be the most affordable. item.description: Dan Campbell guides the Lions through workouts during a spring minicamp. 2022-06-10 Dan Campbell | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions head to South Beach for a Week 9 interconference matchup against a young, rebuilding Miami Dolphins team. We had the pleasure of connecting with Kevin Nogle, the Managing Editor of Phinsider to give us some insight into this Miami team ahead of Sunday’s kickoff. We learned about the local sentiment surrounding head coach Jeff Hafley’s foundational reset, how offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik is tailoring the offense to quarterback Malik Willis, and how Ollie Gordon is handling the backfield workload in De’Von Achane’s absence—plus what Miami needs to do to keep pace with Detroit’s offense. 1. Miami arguably made more changes to their organization than any other team in the NFL this offseason. New head coach, new quarterback, the changing out of long-tenured skill position players—it was a massive overhaul in South Beach. Although the Dolphins are off to a 1-6 start, how much of that was expected from a team that underwent so many changes this offseason? It’s early, but do you get the sense that new head coach Jeff Hafley is the right guy for this rebuild? This year is about setting up the franchise for the future, and while losses are never fun, the struggles were expected. This is the league’s youngest team, and they are facing a steep learning curve. Miami has 14 rookies on the roster, plus another seven first-year players. This is clearly a reset of the team’s foundation, and there will be growing pains. The Dolphins’ schedule has also been brutal this year. They started the year against the Las Vegas Raiders, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, and Minnesota Vikings, not facing a team that had a loss until Week 5 against the Cincinnati Bengals, who were 2-2 coming into that game. Through Week 8, Miami has faced the league’s toughest schedule, with a combined opponent winning percentage of .589. The schedule is not an excuse, but with such a young team, it is another variable to consider. Obviously, things can change, but Hafley has instilled confidence in the fanbase so far. The Mike McDaniel era had some fun moments, but it quickly fell apart and the team never adjusted (and McDaniel still does not seem to have made adjustments as the Los Angeles Chargers struggle this year). I think Hafley’s focus on making the Dolphins physical, allowing the younger players to gain experience, and the team’s ability to make adjustments, learn from mistakes, and continue to fight even in losing situations indicate he is the right guy for this role. Lions fans saw Dan Campbell build a culture out of tough losses back in 2021; that is exactly the phase Hafley and the Dolphins are in right now. 2. They erased their opponent in a way that has never happened before in Division I history. Seven different players hit double figures in the final count. Freshman Anna Minaeva scored 21 points, while Mikaylah Williams added 20 more. Texas Southern shot a dismal 13 percent from the field, making only 8 of 55 attempts while turning the ball over 38 times. This level of domination is rare even in college sports, where mismatches are common. Previous records existed, but this one shatters them. The previous high for a win margin was Baylor’s 140-32 rout over Winthrop in December 2016. That Baylor team was coached by Kim Mulkey, who now leads LSU. item.description: Photo by Warren Little/Getty Images Jon Rahm has produced some extremely impressive golf this week at the Abu Dhabi Championship. Rahm, 31, recently left LIV Golf, and is set to play a full schedule on the DP World Tour next season. However, a win this week in Abu Dhabi would be hugely important for him, with a large amount of world ranking points on offer at Yas Links. Jon Rahm ‘s confirmed exit from LIV Golf last month came as no surprise, and the league has now gone into liquidation. So the Spaniard’s timing could not have been better. Rahm’s full focus will now be on the DP World Tour for the next 12 months and it seems like he could be set to return to his very best form quicker than many expected. Jon Rahm’s verdict on the golf course in Abu Dhabi as he ties the lead Rahm spoke to reporters after firing a second-round 67 to tie for the lead at Yas Links on Friday, and he was asked to give his honest opinion of the condition of the golf course. “ It’s going to be hard to ever find a golf course in better shape than this one, “ he admitted. “ It’s phenomenal what they’ve been able to do. The greens are all perfect. When you give some of the best players in the world perfect greens and fairways that are firm, unless the wind conditions get crazy, you’re going to have some close scores, and that’s what we’re seeing on this course here. “ Overall, the golf course can be quite tricky, especially with certain pin locations, slopes. You can put yourself in difficult spots. But it’s been quite calm, and that’s what’s allowed us to be aggressive. “ He was then asked to rate his performance on day two in Abu Dhabi. “ Pretty good play, “ he replied. “ Only thing to take back would be just a couple of bad tee shots right now, feeling fairly comfortable otherwise. Just there’s been a couple of swings off the tee that were unexpected. But hopefully I can fix that, but otherwise the play has been lovely. “ Jon Rahm is in a very good position after 36 holes of the Abu Dhabi Championship, but he will know that he needs to keep his foot down on the accelerator if he is to have a chance of winning the tournament this weekend.

item.title: Ferrari handed clear ultimatum over driver hierarchy: 'Make Hamilton #1 driver'
item.description: Former Formula 1 world champion Damon Hill has urged Ferrari to establish Lewis Hamilton as its clear number one driver, insisting the seven-time world champion can deliver success if the Italian team gives him its full backing. The 1996 world champion made his position clear on X following the controversial Mexican Grand Prix, where tensions between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc intensified after their opening-lap battle cost Ferrari a potential victory. Hamilton started the race from pole position, with Leclerc third, but the two teammates became involved in a fierce battle through the opening corners. Both went off track at Turn 4, with Leclerc subsequently receiving a five-second penalty for gaining an advantage. Max Verstappen capitalised on the situation to take the lead and eventually win the race, while Hamilton recovered to finish second and Leclerc crossed the line fourth. Hill calls for Ferrari to prioritise Hamilton The incident reignited questions about how Ferrari should manage its two drivers, particularly as Hamilton and Leclerc continue to compete on equal terms. Hill believes the solution is straightforward and has called on Ferrari to make a definitive decision rather than allowing the internal rivalry to continue. Writing on X, the former Williams driver reiterated a position he expressed during the Mexican Grand Prix weekend: "Here is where I stand on the Lewis vs Charles debate, and I made this point on Sunday in Mexico; make Lewis #1 Ferrari driver. Sort it out. Make it clear. Ends all debate. Lewis will deliver for Ferrari. If they back him 100" Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Hill already urged Ferrari to put Hamilton first This is not the first time Hill has advocated for Hamilton to receive preferential treatment at Maranello. Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport ahead of the Mexican Grand Prix, the 1996 world champion questioned Ferrari's decision to maintain equal status between its drivers. "I don't know what's going on within the team, but I get the impression that the drivers are battling it out for the captain's rank. The team have remained neutral, but they really should decide who to back. When Michael Schumacher was in Maranello, the team's attention was focused exclusively on him." Hill then made it clear that Hamilton would be his preferred choice, arguing that Ferrari has never fully committed to the seven-time world champion since his arrival in 2025. "We don't know how much longer Lewis will carry on; he's not in his 20s anymore. After signing him in 2025, Ferrari have never really put him at the heart of the project. I'm convinced that Hamilton can still perform at the very highest level. What he's achieved in Formula 1 is simply extraordinary. So I'd back him."

item.title: The last 18-hole golf course built in Arizona officially goes fully private
item.description: When it opened in February of 2021 , Sterling Grove Golf & Country Club was the first 18-hole golf course built in the greater Phoenix area in five years. In 2026 it remains the most recently built venue in this golfing mecca of close to 200 courses. Now the club in Surprise, Arizona, has gone fully private. That was the plan all along, so everything's right on schedule. The shift was official Nov. 1. The course allowed public play for five years as a semi-private club, but membership has grown to more than 300. The community also has 1,100 homes, so the time was right for the change. "Transitioning to a fully private club allows us to enhance the member experience by focusing on personalized service and exclusive events," general manager Al Larose said in a media release. The 18-hole course by Nicklaus Design is set against a backdrop of the White Tank Mountains west of Phoenix. The course is a parkland-style layout with wide landing areas in fairways and undulating greens. There's an expansive practice area and a large, 18-hole putting course. The club also features three resort-style pools, nine pickleball courts, five tennis courts and bocce courts. The clubhouse features the Flora Spa, a state-of-the-art fitness and movement studio, a full-service restaurant called Copper + Rye, and The Market, which has grab-and-go food items. "Watching Sterling Grove grow from a vision and mounds of dirt into the thriving club and community it is today has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my career,” membership director Hanna Atkins said. “As we celebrate the transition to a fully private club just five years after opening, we're incredibly grateful for the trust and support of our members and excited to continue building on our vision of the modern country club for generations to come." The club said there are still limited membership opportunities available for residents and non-residents. For more golf course and travel stories, go to Golfweek's Golf Life website . Not only that his punting is awful. — REAL HUSKER FAN (@REAL_HUSKER_FAN) October 18, 2026 That’s such a pathetic punt. The Ray Guy Award goes to the best punter in the country. Not only did he make the watch list but he was named the Ray Guy Punter of the Week after averaging 49.8 net yards per punt. He placed four punts inside the Washington 20-yard line. Every punt went at least 40 yards and none of the kicks were returned. He had a 59 yard punt and a 60 yard punt. This is quite the turnaround for the sophomore from Australia. Archie Wilson is a great illustration of why you cannot listen to the emotional reactions from fans. This goes for both the good times and the bad times. Wilson was having some bad times earlier in the month, including when he bent down to catch a low snap and let his knee hit the ground in the game against Oregon. So he has earned some of that criticism. But it says a lot about Archie Wilson that he was able to battle back. Of his 31 punts this season, only four have been returned. That is why you have to wait for the season to play out. SPORTS! SPORTS! JORTS! SPORTS! SPORTS!
